$comment: Triaged entropy ceiling for #544, corrected in #677, lowered in #676, again by the 2026-08-13 paydown, again on 2026-08-18 by the #694 CLI drift fix (291 -> 267, see $driftfix), and again on 2026-08-20 when the floating pin reached CLI 11.3.0 (267 -> 157, the largest single move in this file's history — see $driftfix2). Lower it when the count drops; never raise it to make CI pass. See docs/knowledge/decisions/0012-entropy-ratchet.md for the triage and the categories behind the number. Lowered again on 2026-08-30 when the pin moved to CLI major @12 (157 -> 145, see $driftfix3).
$correction: #677: the exclude list inherited from the CLI covered **/*.test.ts but not **/*.test.js, so all 32 node:test files under npm/scripts/__tests__/ were scanned as ordinary source and reported unreferenced. entropy.excludePatterns is now declared in harness.config.json and the measured count fell 340 -> 308, purely subtractive (the report is otherwise byte-identical).
$reduction: #676: 26 dead documentation links repaired (v6.0.0 Python retirement and the docs/adr -> docs/knowledge/decisions move). 21 of them fall inside docs/, the only tree `harness cleanup` scans, so the measured count fell 308 -> 287. This composes with #677 rather than overlapping it: #677 removed test files from the denominator, #676 removed dead links from the numerator. Re-measured on the merged tree, not derived arithmetically.
$paydown: 2026-08-13 paydown: 15 provably-dead exports removed to create durable headroom (main measured 296 against the 297 ceiling — one finding, and two finished branches waiting on three). Every one was verified category-1 before touching: no importer of the declaring module references it, including via `dist` (the npm package's node:test suite requires `../../dist/*.js`, so npm/src exports that look dead are NOT) and via the ts/src -> npm/src `sync-gate-result.mjs` mirror (`skippedSuffix` looks dead in ts/src and is live in the generated copy). 13 are `export` keyword removals on symbols still used inside their own module — no code deleted, nothing changes at runtime. 2 are real deletions: the `scanFile` thin wrapper in the canary-savant and canary-blackhawk scanners, which had zero consumers anywhere (neither skill's cli.mjs nor its test imports it; both import `scanText`/`scanTextFull`/`scanPaths`). Measured 296 -> 281 on the real tree with `harness cleanup --findings-json`, and the before/after `--json` sets differ by exactly those 15 with ZERO additions and drift unchanged at 24 — purely subtractive, never derived arithmetically. Left deliberately: the 24 drift findings (upstream detector defects, re-verified fence-quoted), the ADR-triaged testkits / fixture projects / spike / five test-only ts/src modules, 15 npm/src exports covered via dist, and `ts/src/cli-common.ts::ensureAscii` — see the wiring finding in ADR 0012.
$driftfix: 2026-08-18, #694 closing: the count fell 281 -> 257 with NO change to this repo. The entire 24-finding `Documentation drift` category disappeared when the CLI moved 11.1.1 -> 11.2.0, which is the `extractFileLinks` fence-awareness defect #694 was waiting on upstream (Intense-Visions/harness-engineering#1342). Measured both ways on the SAME commit (aa36af6) in a clean worktree: 11.1.1 reports 281 with 24 drift findings, 11.2.0 reports 257 with 0. The categories are otherwise identical and dead code is unchanged at 10. This is NOT a paydown — nobody fixed 24 links; a false positive stopped firing, so the ceiling is lowered to match an instrument that got more accurate.
$driftfix_evidence: A category falling to zero and a detector going dark are indistinguishable from the count alone, so the drop was corroborated before the ceiling moved. TWO pieces carry it, and NEITHER is the planted-link smoke check. (1) Per-finding classification: #719 located all 24 findings in their source files and tested fence membership — 56 occurrences, 56 fenced, 0 bare (ADR 0012). That is what identifies the disappeared set as exactly the upstream Class A defect rather than an aggregate coincidence. (2) An independent instrument: `scripts/check_doc_links.mjs` is fence-aware, runs over a LARGER denominator (249 files vs the drift check's docs/** + READMEs), is asserted strict-at-zero in the blocking vitest suite (`ts/test/doc-links.test.ts`), and abstains (exit 3) on an empty walk. Real dead links stay covered by something that does not move when the harness CLI floats. REPEAT THOSE TWO next time this number falls on its own. A planted BARE broken link was also checked and is reported by both versions, but it is only a smoke check and cannot fail by construction: fence awareness is precisely what changed upstream, so a bare link exercises the code path that did not. If a probe is kept, use a fenced/unfenced PAIR.
$headroom: maxFindings is 157 against a measured 147 — 10 findings of deliberate headroom (`maxHeadroom`), the same shape as every previous ceiling (267 against 257, 291 against 281, 297 against 287). This is a TIGHTENING (267 -> 157), not a raise: the forbidden move is lifting maxFindings so a failing check passes, and this lowers it while the measured count is falling. The headroom exists because the ratchet is an ABSOLUTE total, so concurrent branches consume a shared non-renewable budget that none of them can see (#703). A ceiling pinned exactly to the measured count means the next single green PR that adds one finding fails, which is how a blocking gate becomes wallpaper. Lower it again when the count drops; never raise it to make CI pass.
$whatIsGuarded: Read this before trusting the guards. `maxHeadroom` is the SINGLE source for the gap: `scripts/entropy-ratchet.mjs` reads it for both its nudge threshold and the value it recommends, and `ts/test/entropy-ratchet.test.ts` reads it rather than hard-coding a copy. What the offline tests catch: a ceiling RAISED above its last committed value (git-compared, and this is the ratchet's real forbidden move), a hand-edit that moves `maxFindings` without re-measuring `measuredCount`, a missing or range-valued `harnessCli`, and a CLI MAJOR that no longer matches the workflow pin. CLOSED as of #744, and this is what the two drift episodes cost: `harnessCli` is now handed to the ratchet at runtime by the `Resolve harness CLI version` step in `harness-quality.yml`, and any disagreement — including a caller that does not say — is an ABSTENTION (exit 3) rather than a comparison against a ceiling the number is not commensurable with. A floating minor can still move the count, but it can no longer do so quietly. What is STILL not caught: `measuredCount` remains a memory of the last time a human ran the analyzer, so between re-measures it can only be trusted as far as the instrument stamp beside it, and excessive headroom is still only a LOG LINE, never a failure — a codebase that got cleaner must not turn the build red, so nothing forces the ceiling down except a human reading the nudge.
$zeroHeadroom: 2026-09-04, measured while building the #703 delta rule and recorded because it is a LIVE condition, not history: `main` at e923921 measures 145 against a 145 ceiling — ZERO headroom — while this file still read `measuredCount` 135 from 2026-09-01. Nothing was hand-edited and no single PR did this. The count rose 135 -> 145 across the five merges since (#802, #803, #804, #805, #806), each of which fit under 145 individually and was green on its own. That is #703's pathology observed live rather than reconstructed, and it is why `measuredCount` alone is not a safety net: every offline guard stayed green through a 10-finding rise because they compare this file against itself. `maxFindings` is NOT raised — that is this file's one forbidden move, and a stale `measuredCount` is not a reason to commit it. `measuredCount` is corrected to the measurement. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: at zero headroom the absolute backstop fires on the first PR that adds a single finding, whatever its delta. That is the ratchet doing exactly what it says, and the fix is paydown, not a higher ceiling. Paydown is deliberately out of scope for #703. EVIDENCE: both counts produced by CLI 12.2.0 in the same session, head in the working tree and base in a detached worktree at the merge base; the two `--findings-json` outputs are set-identical modulo the path prefix (`diff` of the sorted reports shows only the 10 absolute paths rewritten, zero lines added or removed). The base worktree carried NO `node_modules` and produced that identical set, which is what establishes that the CI base scan does not need an install to be valid.
$deltaRule: 2026-09-04, #703: this ceiling is no longer the only rule. On a pull request the ratchet also scans the MERGE BASE and fails on the delta the branch itself introduced, because an absolute total is order-dependent — headroom is a shared budget no branch can see, and the second of two independently-green branches to merge was failing on findings it did not add (main 294, batch C 296, batch B 297 against a 297 ceiling, C+B merged 299). This ceiling stays as the BACKSTOP and nothing about it changes: a long series of +0 merges could otherwise walk the total upward, and raising maxFindings to make a failing check pass is still the one forbidden move. What is STILL not automated is the line above this one — `measuredCount` remains a memory of the last time a human ran the analyzer. The delta rule removed the order-dependence, not the manual re-measure. See ADR 0012's 2026-09-04 amendment.
$instrument: `harnessCli` is the EXACT version that produced `measuredCount`, and the tests require it to stay a full version rather than a range. The workflows pin `@harness-engineering/cli@11`, a floating major, so the analyzer under this absolute count can change without any commit here — see $driftfix for the time it moved 24 findings, and #744 for the general problem. When the pin resolves to a new version, re-measure and update this file in the same PR rather than letting the two drift apart.
$driftfix2: 2026-08-20, #744: the count fell 257 -> 147 with NO change to this repo, the second consecutive CLI minor to move it. The floating `@harness-engineering/cli@11` pin resolved to 11.3.0 and the dead-code false-positive model changed again. Measured both ways on the SAME commit (c8f412a) in a clean worktree: 11.2.0 reports 257, 11.3.0 reports 147. This one is worse than $driftfix, because for four days the ceiling stood at 267 against a real 147 — 120 findings of slack on a gate that had just been deliberately TIGHTENED to 267. It would have taken a 45% increase in entropy to turn CI red. Nothing was broken and no test failed: as $whatIsGuarded predicted in writing, every offline guard compares this file against itself and a floating MINOR clears the CLI MAJOR check by construction. The ceiling is lowered to 157 (147 + 10 headroom). CONFIRMED by CI on PR #746: the `validate` job resolved `@harness-engineering/cli@11` to 11.3.0 and reported 147 — an exact match with the fresh-worktree measurement.
$driftfix2_evidence: Three pieces, and the planted positive is the one that does the real work — a falling count cannot distinguish 'the code got cleaner' from 'the detector went dark'. (1) PURELY SUBTRACTIVE: 31 files stopped being flagged and ZERO were newly flagged; the per-file counts of the 47 that remain either held or fell. (2) PLANTED POSITIVE, in the shape this file's predecessor asked for: three unambiguously-dead exports appended to `ts/src/core/pattern-matcher.ts` — a LIVE file that 11.3.0 reports as clean — moved the total 147 -> 150 and the file 0 -> 3. That kills the per-file-dedup hypothesis, which the raw numbers alone look exactly like: nearly every shared file collapsed to exactly 1 finding, and a granularity change would have produced the same shape. The probe MUST go in a live, currently-clean file; in a new file the file itself is dead and a +3 cannot be attributed. (3) THE DISAPPEARED SET IS SHIPPED CODE: `ts/src/guardian/adjudication.ts` (6), `analysis-emit.ts` (5), `github-paging.ts` (4), `pattern-matcher.ts`, and the per-skill `scanner.mjs`/`rules.mjs` trees — the test-only-consumer and workflow-invoked classes ADR 0012 already documents as known false positives. REPEAT ALL THREE next time this number falls on its own.
$driftfix3: 2026-08-30, harness CLI 11.3.0 -> 12.1.0 (the @11 -> @12 pin bump): the count fell 147 -> 135 with NO change to this repo — the THIRD consecutive CLI release to move it, and the first one that was caught before it landed rather than days afterwards. Measured both ways on the SAME commit (3659ea9) in a clean worktree: 11.3.0 reports 147, 12.1.0 reports 135. The entire 12-finding delta is in `dead-code`; `drift` and `patterns` are 0 under both, so the #694 fence fix is unaffected. This is NOT a paydown — nobody removed 12 dead exports; the analyzer's false-positive model changed again. Ceiling lowered to 145 (135 + the 10 `maxHeadroom` this file has always carried). Upstream 12.0.0 declares NO breaking changes (its changeset has only Minor and Patch sections), which is precisely why the number moving anyway is worth recording here: the release notes are not the instrument.
$driftfix3_evidence: The guard worked, and that is the headline. Unlike $driftfix and $driftfix2 — both found by hand, days late — `requireMatchingInstrument` (#744) ABSTAINED (exit 3) the moment the report was produced by 12.1.0 against a ceiling calibrated at 11.3.0, and `ts/test/entropy-ratchet.test.ts` went red on the MAJOR check the moment the workflow pin moved to @12. A major bump can no longer widen this gate quietly. The three pieces $driftfix2_evidence demands were still run, because a FALLING count cannot distinguish 'the analyzer got more accurate' from 'the detector went dark': (1) PLANTED POSITIVE, the load-bearing one — three unambiguously-dead exports appended to `ts/src/core/pattern-matcher.ts` (a live file both versions report clean, as this protocol requires: in a NEW file the file itself is dead and a +3 cannot be attributed) moved 11.3.0 147 -> 150 and 12.1.0 135 -> 138. Both majors detect planted dead code identically, so 12.1.0 is not blind to the class. (2) CATEGORY ISOLATION: `cleanup -t dead-code|drift|patterns` reports 147/0/0 under 11.3.0 and 135/0/0 under 12.1.0 — the move is confined to one category rather than spread, which is the shape of a false-positive model change and not of a scanner that lost files. (3) EVERY OTHER CHECK IS UNMOVED: of the 11 read-only subcommands canary's workflows invoke, 10 are byte-identical across the two majors — `check-arch --json` is md5-identical, `check-perf` is byte-identical at 227 issues across 47,514 bytes. A scanner that had gone dark on a file set would have moved `check-perf` too, since it walks the same denominator. NOT re-verified: the per-file disappeared set. `harness cleanup` hard-truncates its listing at 10 items with no full-output flag, so the file-by-file subtraction $driftfix2 performed could not be repeated here. That is a real gap in this evidence relative to the last one — the planted positive and the category isolation carry it instead. Filed as a request upstream.
$driftfix4: 2026-09-01, harness CLI 12.1.0 -> 12.2.0 (the floating `@12` pin resolving forward, found by the SessionStart tooling-rot siren before this PR merged): the count did NOT move. 135 under both, measured on the same commit (6a37557) in the same clean worktree this file's protocol requires. This is the FIRST release in four where the number held, and it is recorded anyway because `requireMatchingInstrument` (#744) compares instrument IDENTITY, not the number: leaving `harnessCli` at 12.1.0 while CI resolves `@12` to 12.2.0 would ABSTAIN this gate (exit 3) on every run, converting a passing ratchet into a permanent no-op. An unmoved count still needs a current instrument stamp — the same lesson `$remeasure2` recorded on the perf side, now confirmed on this one. `maxFindings` is UNCHANGED at 145: the measured count did not move, so there is nothing to lower, and raising is this file's one forbidden move.
$driftfix4_evidence: SET-equality, not byte-equality, is the load-bearing check here, and the distinction mattered. The two `cleanup --findings-json` outputs are the same length (1,501 B) but have DIFFERENT md5s: `ts/src/analysis/reachability.ts` moved position in the listing. A byte-comparison alone would have reported a change where the finding set is identical; `diff` shows exactly one line moved and zero lines added or removed. CATEGORY ISOLATION re-run as the protocol demands: `cleanup -t dead-code|drift|patterns` reports 135/0/0 under BOTH majors, so the #694 fence fix is still holding and no category silently emptied. EVERY OTHER CHECK UNMOVED: `check-perf` is byte-identical across the two at 227 issues and 47,514 bytes (same md5) — a scanner that had gone dark on a file set would have moved check-perf too, since it walks the same denominator. NOT re-run: the planted positive. `$driftfix2_evidence` requires it when a count FALLS, because a fall cannot distinguish a more accurate analyzer from a dark detector. This count did not fall, and an unchanged set under an unchanged category breakdown is not the ambiguous shape the probe exists to resolve. If the next release moves this number in either direction, the planted positive is mandatory again.
